questions.question: Is the UI modern, easy to use, easy to navigate, and visually appealing for the target persona?
visibleEvidence: All 10 contact sheets show the same full-height rounded-card renderer repeated across communities and workflow states.
Representative full-resolution rows b25-v4-row-074, b25-v4-row-161, b25-v4-row-193, and b25-v4-row-194 show dense stacked panels with primary actions embedded in repeated cards.
questions.why: The screens are readable and mostly unclipped, but they do not feel like differentiated production product screens. The dominant experience is a uniform workflow-card scaffold rather than modern task-specific surfaces.
questions.requiredFix: Replace the generic stacked-card renderer with screen-specific product surfaces such as feeds, inbox threads, event detail pages, payment receipts, export wizards, care request forms, and review queues.

questions.question: Is information architecture centered on real community jobs and content?
visibleEvidence: Community nouns are present, such as Garden Club events, Masjid announcements, HOA documents, and Data Portability exports.
The visible structure is still repeated workflow cards with sections like Ready to save, Ready to publish, Member state, Receiver state, Local package details, and Member tools.
questions.why: The content has domain labels, but navigation and page structure are still organized around workflow state cards and validation concepts rather than natural community destinations and jobs.
questions.requiredFix: Reframe home and workflow entry around community sections and objects: event calendars, inboxes, document libraries, donation history, request queues, rosters, and export/recovery workspaces.

questions.question: Does copy sound product-native rather than workflow/spec/test language?
visibleEvidence: Rows repeatedly show phrasing such as Decide whether..., Decide what to save..., Ready to save, Ready to publish, Receiver state, Member state, and Review member-visible summary.
Row b25-v4-row-074 says Decide whether the request should be approved, rejected, revised, or sent back for changes on a member care request screen.
questions.why: The copy often describes the workflow contract rather than speaking as a finished product to the user in the current task.
questions.requiredFix: Rewrite user-facing copy as domain-native product language, using concrete object state and next steps; remove UX-contract phrases from visible screens.

questions.question: Are hierarchy, spacing, typography, color, and component variety shippable?
visibleEvidence: Typography is legible and spacing is generally stable, but nearly every screen uses oversized rounded cards, chips, icon badges, and one dominant hue per community.
Action/review states often look like the same template with a different title rather than distinct forms, detail views, receipts, or inbox screens.
questions.why: The visual system is coherent but too monotonous and template-bound for a production UX bar across 68 workflow/persona paths.
questions.requiredFix: Introduce task-appropriate layouts and component variety: compact lists, real forms, timelines, tables/checklists where appropriate, receipts, message bubbles, document rows, and richer status/history treatments.

questions.question: Is repeated-card fatigue absent?
visibleEvidence: Rows 001-183 are overwhelmingly repeated card stacks; rows 190-195 repeat the same Masjid announcement card flow for multi-persona proof.
The same Ready to..., Decide..., chips, and bottom primary-button construction appears across garden, book club, soccer, HOA, mosque, chess, camera, platform, ad-off, and export workflows.
questions.why: The repeated-card shell is the dominant user experience, so the app still reads as a generic workflow renderer with domain copy pasted into it.
questions.requiredFix: Create domain-native primary surfaces for each workflow family and reserve cards for individual items, not the entire screen architecture.

questions.question: Does each screen provide concrete content and lifecycle actions a real user needs?
visibleEvidence: Many rows include concrete content such as dates, amounts, venues, counts, authors, receipts, and privacy chips.

Deterministic lifecycle evidence still fails for book-search-ai-digest, hoa-owner-notification, platform-messages-entry, export-import-replay, platform-message-stream, export-protected-redaction, and export-import-preview.
Workflow/persona evidence fails for export-protected-redaction / owner.
questions.why: The screenshots often include useful details, but B25 cannot pass while lifecycle scorecards and one workflow/persona scorecard still fail, and several result states remain generic.
questions.requiredFix: Add screenshot-proven concrete object context and persistent result/receiver states for failed workflows, then rerun lifecycle and LLM review gates.

questions.question: Is `wf_multi-persona-workflow-evidence` a support/evidence surface where production workflow lifecycle proof is not required, and is its screenshot evidence still present?
questions.why: This row is a support/evidence surface; lifecycle proof is not required and screenshot evidence is present.

acceptanceCriteria: The `wf_multi-persona-workflow-evidence` screenshots show the concrete domain object/context for `member`.
The user can see enough domain-specific decision information before acting.
The UI provides semantic primary action and the needed alternate/change/reject/defer path; `Cancel` alone cannot stand in for a real decline/reject/change response.

The semantic interaction model names the correct user decision and the right domain actions for `wf_multi-persona-workflow-evidence`; generic accept/cancel or submit/cancel actions do not satisfy this criterion.
The post-action screen shows a persistent result/receipt/status state that can be understood later.
The receiver/read-only/continuation state is visible where another persona or later state is part of the workflow.
The workflow lifecycle scorecard passes with no missing lifecycle groups.

evidenceIntegrityCriteria.title: No unresolved blocker or major findings

remediationCriteria.title: Failed prior iterations have proof of remediation

Representative full-resolution rows b25-v4-row-074, b25-v4-row-161, b25-v4-row-193, and b25-v4-row-194 show dense stacked panels with primary actions embedded in repeated cards.

failingDirectQuestions.question: Is information architecture centered on real community jobs and content?
failingDirectQuestions.why: The content has domain labels, but navigation and page structure are still organized around workflow state cards and validation concepts rather than natural community destinations and jobs.
failingDirectQuestions.requiredFix: Reframe home and workflow entry around community sections and objects: event calendars, inboxes, document libraries, donation history, request queues, rosters, and export/recovery workspaces.
visibleEvidence: Community nouns are present, such as Garden Club events, Masjid announcements, HOA documents, and Data Portability exports.
The visible structure is still repeated workflow cards with sections like Ready to save, Ready to publish, Member state, Receiver state, Local package details, and Member tools.

failingDirectQuestions.question: Does copy sound product-native rather than workflow/spec/test language?
failingDirectQuestions.why: The copy often describes the workflow contract rather than speaking as a finished product to the user in the current task.
failingDirectQuestions.requiredFix: Rewrite user-facing copy as domain-native product language, using concrete object state and next steps; remove UX-contract phrases from visible screens.
visibleEvidence: Rows repeatedly show phrasing such as Decide whether..., Decide what to save..., Ready to save, Ready to publish, Receiver state, Member state, and Review member-visible summary.
Row b25-v4-row-074 says Decide whether the request should be approved, rejected, revised, or sent back for changes on a member care request screen.

failingDirectQuestions.question: Are hierarchy, spacing, typography, color, and component variety shippable?
failingDirectQuestions.why: The visual system is coherent but too monotonous and template-bound for a production UX bar across 68 workflow/persona paths.
failingDirectQuestions.requiredFix: Introduce task-appropriate layouts and component variety: compact lists, real forms, timelines, tables/checklists where appropriate, receipts, message bubbles, document rows, and richer status/history treatments.
visibleEvidence: Typography is legible and spacing is generally stable, but nearly every screen uses oversized rounded cards, chips, icon badges, and one dominant hue per community.
Action/review states often look like the same template with a different title rather than distinct forms, detail views, receipts, or inbox screens.

failingDirectQuestions.question: Is repeated-card fatigue absent?
failingDirectQuestions.why: The repeated-card shell is the dominant user experience, so the app still reads as a generic workflow renderer with domain copy pasted into it.
failingDirectQuestions.requiredFix: Create domain-native primary surfaces for each workflow family and reserve cards for individual items, not the entire screen architecture.
visibleEvidence: Rows 001-183 are overwhelmingly repeated card stacks; rows 190-195 repeat the same Masjid announcement card flow for multi-persona proof.
The same Ready to..., Decide..., chips, and bottom primary-button construction appears across garden, book club, soccer, HOA, mosque, chess, camera, platform, ad-off, and export workflows.

failingDirectQuestions.question: Does each screen provide concrete content and lifecycle actions a real user needs?
failingDirectQuestions.why: The screenshots often include useful details, but B25 cannot pass while lifecycle scorecards and one workflow/persona scorecard still fail, and several result states remain generic.
failingDirectQuestions.requiredFix: Add screenshot-proven concrete object context and persistent result/receiver states for failed workflows, then rerun lifecycle and LLM review gates.
visibleEvidence: Many rows include concrete content such as dates, amounts, venues, counts, authors, receipts, and privacy chips.

Deterministic lifecycle evidence still fails for book-search-ai-digest, hoa-owner-notification, platform-messages-entry, export-import-replay, platform-message-stream, export-protected-redaction, and export-import-preview.
Workflow/persona evidence fails for export-protected-redaction / owner.

remediationTickets.title: Screens are organized around community content and jobs-to-be-done
remediationTickets.directQuestion: Is the overall information architecture organized around community content and real jobs-to-be-done instead of workflow lists or validation surfaces?
remediationTickets.whyItFailed: holistic direct-question answers are missing, weak, partial, or blocking: b25-v4-pass-24-modern-easy-appealing, b25-v4-pass-24-community-ia, b25-v4-pass-24-copy-product-native, b25-v4-pass-24-visual-system, b25-v4-pass-24-repeated-card-fatigue, b25-v4-pass-24-concrete-content-lifecycle-actions.
remediationTickets.requiredOutcome: Rebuild home and primary screens around community content and user jobs.
remediationTickets.workerReadiness: no concrete implementation work item was generated; planner must inspect the direct-question failure before assigning a worker
remediationTickets.firstRequiredStep: Review failing direct questions and add screen/workflow/persona-specific evidence before implementation.
implementationBlockedBy: The ticket lacks row-level implementation evidence.

failingDirectQuestions.question: Is the UI modern, easy to use, easy to navigate, and visually appealing for the target persona?
failingDirectQuestions.why: The screens are readable and mostly unclipped, but they do not feel like differentiated production product screens. The dominant experience is a uniform workflow-card scaffold rather than modern task-specific surfaces.
failingDirectQuestions.requiredFix: Replace the generic stacked-card renderer with screen-specific product surfaces such as feeds, inbox threads, event detail pages, payment receipts, export wizards, care request forms, and review queues.
visibleEvidence: All 10 contact sheets show the same full-height rounded-card renderer repeated across communities and workflow states.
Representative full-resolution rows b25-v4-row-074, b25-v4-row-161, b25-v4-row-193, and b25-v4-row-194 show dense stacked panels with primary actions embedded in repeated cards.

failingDirectQuestions.question: Is information architecture centered on real community jobs and content?
failingDirectQuestions.why: The content has domain labels, but navigation and page structure are still organized around workflow state cards and validation concepts rather than natural community destinations and jobs.
failingDirectQuestions.requiredFix: Reframe home and workflow entry around community sections and objects: event calendars, inboxes, document libraries, donation history, request queues, rosters, and export/recovery workspaces.
visibleEvidence: Community nouns are present, such as Garden Club events, Masjid announcements, HOA documents, and Data Portability exports.
The visible structure is still repeated workflow cards with sections like Ready to save, Ready to publish, Member state, Receiver state, Local package details, and Member tools.

failingDirectQuestions.question: Does copy sound product-native rather than workflow/spec/test language?
failingDirectQuestions.why: The copy often describes the workflow contract rather than speaking as a finished product to the user in the current task.
failingDirectQuestions.requiredFix: Rewrite user-facing copy as domain-native product language, using concrete object state and next steps; remove UX-contract phrases from visible screens.
visibleEvidence: Rows repeatedly show phrasing such as Decide whether..., Decide what to save..., Ready to save, Ready to publish, Receiver state, Member state, and Review member-visible summary.
Row b25-v4-row-074 says Decide whether the request should be approved, rejected, revised, or sent back for changes on a member care request screen.

failingDirectQuestions.question: Are hierarchy, spacing, typography, color, and component variety shippable?
failingDirectQuestions.why: The visual system is coherent but too monotonous and template-bound for a production UX bar across 68 workflow/persona paths.
failingDirectQuestions.requiredFix: Introduce task-appropriate layouts and component variety: compact lists, real forms, timelines, tables/checklists where appropriate, receipts, message bubbles, document rows, and richer status/history treatments.
visibleEvidence: Typography is legible and spacing is generally stable, but nearly every screen uses oversized rounded cards, chips, icon badges, and one dominant hue per community.
Action/review states often look like the same template with a different title rather than distinct forms, detail views, receipts, or inbox screens.

failingDirectQuestions.question: Is repeated-card fatigue absent?
failingDirectQuestions.why: The repeated-card shell is the dominant user experience, so the app still reads as a generic workflow renderer with domain copy pasted into it.
failingDirectQuestions.requiredFix: Create domain-native primary surfaces for each workflow family and reserve cards for individual items, not the entire screen architecture.
visibleEvidence: Rows 001-183 are overwhelmingly repeated card stacks; rows 190-195 repeat the same Masjid announcement card flow for multi-persona proof.
The same Ready to..., Decide..., chips, and bottom primary-button construction appears across garden, book club, soccer, HOA, mosque, chess, camera, platform, ad-off, and export workflows.

failingDirectQuestions.question: Does each screen provide concrete content and lifecycle actions a real user needs?
failingDirectQuestions.why: The screenshots often include useful details, but B25 cannot pass while lifecycle scorecards and one workflow/persona scorecard still fail, and several result states remain generic.
failingDirectQuestions.requiredFix: Add screenshot-proven concrete object context and persistent result/receiver states for failed workflows, then rerun lifecycle and LLM review gates.
visibleEvidence: Many rows include concrete content such as dates, amounts, venues, counts, authors, receipts, and privacy chips.

Deterministic lifecycle evidence still fails for book-search-ai-digest, hoa-owner-notification, platform-messages-entry, export-import-replay, platform-message-stream, export-protected-redaction, and export-import-preview.
Workflow/persona evidence fails for export-protected-redaction / owner.

failingDirectQuestions.question: Is the UI modern, easy to use, easy to navigate, and visually appealing for the target persona?
failingDirectQuestions.why: The screens are readable and mostly unclipped, but they do not feel like differentiated production product screens. The dominant experience is a uniform workflow-card scaffold rather than modern task-specific surfaces.
failingDirectQuestions.requiredFix: Replace the generic stacked-card renderer with screen-specific product surfaces such as feeds, inbox threads, event detail pages, payment receipts, export wizards, care request forms, and review queues.
visibleEvidence: All 10 contact sheets show the same full-height rounded-card renderer repeated across communities and workflow states.
Representative full-resolution rows b25-v4-row-074, b25-v4-row-161, b25-v4-row-193, and b25-v4-row-194 show dense stacked panels with primary actions embedded in repeated cards.

failingDirectQuestions.question: Is information architecture centered on real community jobs and content?
failingDirectQuestions.why: The content has domain labels, but navigation and page structure are still organized around workflow state cards and validation concepts rather than natural community destinations and jobs.
failingDirectQuestions.requiredFix: Reframe home and workflow entry around community sections and objects: event calendars, inboxes, document libraries, donation history, request queues, rosters, and export/recovery workspaces.
visibleEvidence: Community nouns are present, such as Garden Club events, Masjid announcements, HOA documents, and Data Portability exports.
The visible structure is still repeated workflow cards with sections like Ready to save, Ready to publish, Member state, Receiver state, Local package details, and Member tools.

failingDirectQuestions.question: Does copy sound product-native rather than workflow/spec/test language?
failingDirectQuestions.why: The copy often describes the workflow contract rather than speaking as a finished product to the user in the current task.
failingDirectQuestions.requiredFix: Rewrite user-facing copy as domain-native product language, using concrete object state and next steps; remove UX-contract phrases from visible screens.
visibleEvidence: Rows repeatedly show phrasing such as Decide whether..., Decide what to save..., Ready to save, Ready to publish, Receiver state, Member state, and Review member-visible summary.
Row b25-v4-row-074 says Decide whether the request should be approved, rejected, revised, or sent back for changes on a member care request screen.

failingDirectQuestions.question: Are hierarchy, spacing, typography, color, and component variety shippable?
failingDirectQuestions.why: The visual system is coherent but too monotonous and template-bound for a production UX bar across 68 workflow/persona paths.
failingDirectQuestions.requiredFix: Introduce task-appropriate layouts and component variety: compact lists, real forms, timelines, tables/checklists where appropriate, receipts, message bubbles, document rows, and richer status/history treatments.
visibleEvidence: Typography is legible and spacing is generally stable, but nearly every screen uses oversized rounded cards, chips, icon badges, and one dominant hue per community.
Action/review states often look like the same template with a different title rather than distinct forms, detail views, receipts, or inbox screens.

failingDirectQuestions.question: Is repeated-card fatigue absent?
failingDirectQuestions.why: The repeated-card shell is the dominant user experience, so the app still reads as a generic workflow renderer with domain copy pasted into it.
failingDirectQuestions.requiredFix: Create domain-native primary surfaces for each workflow family and reserve cards for individual items, not the entire screen architecture.
visibleEvidence: Rows 001-183 are overwhelmingly repeated card stacks; rows 190-195 repeat the same Masjid announcement card flow for multi-persona proof.
The same Ready to..., Decide..., chips, and bottom primary-button construction appears across garden, book club, soccer, HOA, mosque, chess, camera, platform, ad-off, and export workflows.

failingDirectQuestions.question: Does each screen provide concrete content and lifecycle actions a real user needs?
failingDirectQuestions.why: The screenshots often include useful details, but B25 cannot pass while lifecycle scorecards and one workflow/persona scorecard still fail, and several result states remain generic.
failingDirectQuestions.requiredFix: Add screenshot-proven concrete object context and persistent result/receiver states for failed workflows, then rerun lifecycle and LLM review gates.
visibleEvidence: Many rows include concrete content such as dates, amounts, venues, counts, authors, receipts, and privacy chips.

Deterministic lifecycle evidence still fails for book-search-ai-digest, hoa-owner-notification, platform-messages-entry, export-import-replay, platform-message-stream, export-protected-redaction, and export-import-preview.
Workflow/persona evidence fails for export-protected-redaction / owner.
